title: fix(service-storage): a file field's accept/maxSize refusal answers 400 ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT
body:
Fixes #21730
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`FileConstraintError` (`packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.ts`) declares `status = 400`, as `FileFieldBulkWriteError` in the same file already does. It also carries `field` and `constraint` (`'accept' | 'maxSize'`) as members, set by the constructor, and both throw sites in `assertFileConstraints` pass them. The constructor is now `new FileConstraintError(field, constraint, message)`, and the `FileConstraint` type is exported beside the class. The message text is byte-identical.

A file field's `accept` / `maxSize` refusal now answers `400 ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT` with a sentence naming the field and the constraint. Before, it answered the sanitised `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`. The accept set does not change: the same files are refused, and a refused write still persists no row and claims no file.

## Measured at the `/api/v1/data` door

Real stack (`bootStack` + `StorageServicePlugin`), object `ffc_doc` with `doc: { type: 'file', accept: ['.pdf'], maxSize: 10 }`, `sys_file` rows seeded under a system context.

| write | before (`ff29410e`) | after (`415514d0`) |
|---|---|---|
| POST, `text/plain` file | `500 {"error":"Internal server error","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}` | `400 {"error":"File type 'text/plain' is not permitted by the accept list declared for 'doc' (.pdf)","code":"ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT","object":"ffc_doc"}` |
| POST, 5005-byte PDF | `500`, same body | `400 {"error":"File exceeds the maximum size declared for 'doc' (5005 bytes > 10 bytes)","code":"ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT","object":"ffc_doc"}` |
| PATCH onto the 5005-byte PDF | `500`, same body | `400`, same body as the POST |
| POST, 6-byte PDF (control) | `201` | `201` |

Read-back on both sides: neither refused POST wrote a row, and no refused write claimed its `sys_file` (`ref_object` / `ref_id` / `ref_field` stay null).

## The PM's mechanism hypotheses, measured

- **H1 holds.** `ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT` is registered at `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:506`. No ledger edit.
- **H2 holds.** The 400 body carries exactly the keys `error`, `code` and `object`. `field` and `constraint` are declared on the error, but the declared-status passthrough (`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts`, 4xx arm of `classifyDataError`) forwards only the bounded message, the narrowed `code` and the route's `object`. The exported `mapDataError` wrapper can add a producer-marked `userMessage`, and this error sets none. So on the wire, the field and the constraint are named by the message only. Triage's direction asked for members "the thrown-error resolver forwards". That half is not met, because no such member exists without a `packages/types` edit, and this card was fenced away from that file. See Acceptance notes.
- **H3 holds.** Both messages reach the body byte-identical (`error === thrown message` for accept, maxSize and the update). The 4xx arm strips only a leading restatement of the producer's own code, which this message has none of. It then applies the 500-character truncation bound. No leak heuristic runs on this arm.
- **H4 holds.** Create and update reach the same throw site (`applyCopyOnClaim`, called from both `beforeInsert` and `beforeUpdate`). Both are pinned, at the unit seam and at the door.

## Tests

- `packages/services/service-storage/src/file-reference-lifecycle.test.ts`: the accept and maxSize create refusals and a new update refusal each assert `{ code: 'ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT', status: 400, field: 'image', constraint }`, that the message names the field, and that no row was written or file claimed. 51/51 pass. The whole `@objectstack/service-storage` suite passes 634/634 (41 files), and `typecheck` (including `check:test-typecheck`) exits 0. Both at `9251e230`.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/file-field-constraint-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` (new): the door-level pin from the table above, in 5 cases. Both refusals, the update refusal, the small-PDF control, and an update-onto-a-permitted-file control. Each refusal asserts `code` and `status` and reads back the rows and the `sys_file` ownership columns. 5/5 pass, at `415514d0` (the `main` merge that followed brought only `packages/cli` files). The dogfood `tsc --noEmit` exits 0 and its program lists this file.
- **Ablation** (committed fix first, so restore points at HEAD). I planted `readonly ablation21730 = true;` in place of `readonly status = 400;` on `FileConstraintError`, using `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor 1 → 0, blob `632a803a` → `487a00f9`). Then I rebuilt `service-storage`. `ablation-dist-preflight` proved the marker present in 2 built files. Results:
  - Unit: **3 failed / 48 passed**. The three refusal cases failed with `expected Error: File exceeds the maximum size decl… to match object { code: 'ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT', …(3) }`.
  - Dogfood: **3 failed / 2 passed**. The three refusals failed with `{"error":"Internal server error","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}: expected 500 to be 400`. Both controls stayed green.
  - Restore: blob after restore `632a803a` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, the whole-tree `git status --porcelain` is empty, and the rebuild's preflight in `--absent` mode shows the marker absent from all 6 built files. The unit (51/51) and dogfood (5/5) re-runs passed.
  - The ablation exercised the status assertions. The no-row read-backs were not ablated separately, because no product mutation answers 400 and lands the row. What shows the readers can see a landed write is the control cases: the same `rowsNamed` / `owner` readers return the row and its claimed file.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `9251e230` derived 70 commands. I ran every one, recording each exit code. `--ran` reports: `70 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 68 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (2 DERIVED from a recorded exit 3)`.

- NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, reason: PREREQUISITE NOT MET, because 33 packages outside this diff's closure have no `dist/`. Supplementary reading: `require()` of `service-storage/dist/index.cjs` and `import()` of `dist/index.js` both load, and each constructs a `FileConstraintError` with `status: 400` and both members.
- NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:i18n`, reason: PREREQUISITE NOT MET (unbuilt config imports). This diff touches no translation bundle or label.
- `node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` first exited 3, because its pinned fixture commit was absent from this shallow clone. It exited 0 after `git fetch --depth=1` of that commit.

## Acceptance notes

- **QA checklist clause, routed to the next run, not edited here.** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/attachments-storage.json`, item `attachments-storage.field-accept-maxsize-server-enforced`, carries a knownGap and clause 2. Both predict the sanitised 500 and say a measured 4xx carrying `ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT` means "revise this clause with the measurement". The `FOLLOW-UPS.md` row D13 describes the same 500. The item's own clause routes that revision to the next QA run. The message prose that clause greps (`'exceeds the maximum size declared for'`, `'not permitted by the accept list declared for'`) is unchanged.
- **The field and the constraint are on the wire through the message only.** That is what the door forwards today (H2). Forwarding `field` / `constraint` as structured body members would take a `packages/types` change (an `ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT` arm in `structuredCodeAnswer`, or a generic declared-4xx detail channel). That file belongs to another lane, so the seat routes it. Nothing measured here reads such a member.
- **Observation, not filed:** a declared-4xx refusal at the data door still prints `[REST] Unhandled error` with a stack (`logUnexpectedRouteError` treats only 403/404/409/502/503 and a few query codes as expected). This refusal shares that with `FILE_FIELD_BULK_WRITE_REFUSED` and every hook-declared 400. It is log noise only, and the wire is unaffected. Carrier: none.
- **Observation, not filed:** `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx` (Media Types) says file constraints "are configured at the storage-provider layer, not on the field". `accept` / `maxSize` have been declared on `FieldSchema` and enforced on write since 17.0. This was already false before this change, which does not touch it. Carrier: none.
- The changeset is `patch`. The exported `FileConstraintError` constructor gains two leading parameters. The only constructor in the repository is the module's own throw sites.

## Patch round 1

_Appended by the seat (`domain:services#1`, `session_011K3zqE8Pv1Evw5hc8tZCnN`) from the dev's patch-round report `5981408643`, after seat review `5981327964`._

- **`content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`, "Media Types" paragraph** (`f18345a4`). The sentence saying file constraints "are configured at the storage-provider layer, not on the field" is replaced. The paragraph now says that `accept` and `maxSize` apply to the media family (`file`, `image`, `avatar`, `video`, `audio`), and what each one means, following the spec's own `.describe()` text: `accept` is the permitted upload types as MIME types or extensions, offered to the file picker and enforced on write. `maxSize` is the maximum file size in bytes, enforced on write against the stored file size. It also says a create or update whose referenced file violates either is refused with `400 ERR_FILE_CONSTRAINT`, and that the message names the field and the constraint. It keeps the true half: storage itself is configured at the storage-provider layer. No other sentence on the page mentions `accept` or `maxSize`, so nothing else on the page changed.
- **`main` merged** at `aa33b2e3`. It brought 5 commits, and none of them touches this PR's files.
- **Gates** at `aa33b2e3`. `dispatch-gates --commands` derives 95 commands. The doc edit adds 25 of them, and the dev ran those 25 plus `check:nul-bytes`: all exited 0. The other 70 codes are the code-half results recorded at `9251e230`, reused as recorded. `--ran` reports: 95 derived, 93 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n`, each exit 3 with its prerequisite not met, unchanged from the code half), 0 UNRUN.
- **Acceptance notes revision:** the `field-types.mdx` observation above is resolved by this round.
